source.title: Bald eagle
source.quote: Females are about 25% larger than males, averaging as much as 5.6 kg (12 lb), and against the males' average weight of 4.1 kg (9.0 lb).

mass_kg.note: Average adult female. Range is the standard +/-10%; the article's 3-6.3 kg range includes males.

source.title: Bald eagle
source.quote: The bald eagle has a body length of 70–102 cm (28–40 in).

size_m.note: Body length, not wingspan (1.8-2.3 m). Upper figure, since females are the larger sex; the source gives only a range.

source.title: Bald eagle
source.quote: It reaches speeds of 56–70 km/h (35–43 mph) when gliding and flapping, and about 48 km/h (30 mph) while carrying fish.

top_speed_mps.note: 70 km/h = 19.44 m/s, the upper figure of powered flight. Dives reach 120-160 km/h, but the article says it seldom dives vertically.

source.title: Bald eagle
source.quote: In one instance, a bald eagle was observed carrying 6.8 kg (15 lb) mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) fawn.

attack_force_n.note: Stand-in: a carried load as force, 6.8 kg x 9.80665 = 66.69 N (like the elephant's trunk lift). No talon force in newtons is published. Probably low for a strike. Range is +/-50%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published strike rate found for this animal; category default (estimate 1 of 2).

endurance_s.note: No published fighting endurance found for this animal; category default (estimate 2 of 2).

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 4: territorial, steals prey from other predators and attacks dogs and vultures at carcasses.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 2: congregates in winter, but each eagle hunts for itself.
